research_notes: Follow-up: identify footwear, towing/roadside and parts-supply employers; obtain public historical employment/contract evidence for hours, breaks, legal employer and control. Reconcile overlapping 1989–2000 and 1998–2000 descriptions before any calculation.

2026-09-29 initial pass: compared current APH indexed biography, 2017 Parliamentary Handbook indexed entry, full 29 September 2010 first speech, ALP biography and ABC 2013 candidate guide. Direct APH and ANU PDF opens failed; no access controls bypassed.

Targeted searches for bootmaker employer, diesel-parts employer, RACV, full-time work and agriculture adviser did not identify the missing companies or admissible hours evidence. Numerous unrelated Rob Mitchell professional profiles and overseas full-time references excluded. Repeat only with a new employer or archive lead.

Historical handbook adds 1987–1989 roadside work omitted from current APH list; omission is not evidence that work did not occur. Speech confirms sequence but cannot prove RACV was employer or fix every contract date. Transport-role titles alone do not prove private control of unidentified entities.

Campaigns in 1999, 2006 and 2007 and party participation described in first speech are political activity, not presumed paid employment. Professional membership and volunteer work likewise are not substantive paid employment. No unsupported zero or uninterrupted duration entered; initial record remains blocked.

2026-10-02 follow-up: added apprenticeship daily-hours recollection and October2007 cessation of political advisory work, qualifying the existing2006–2010 envelope. State Parliament profile confirms term and supplies 27February2003 first-speech archive lead, but legacy endpoint unavailable. Searches for footwear/diesel/parts employers and ministerial work found no company identity or weekly-hours evidence; overseas BMW, diesel social-media and medical namesakes excluded. Next: accessible Victorian2003 Hansard p56 onward for employer clues, and post-election adviser reappointment record; do not repeat generic company searches without a new lead. Both headline totals remain unknown.

2026-10-03 follow-up: a first-person 18 April 2016 parliamentary speech adds truck driving and vehicle servicing to the previously recorded transport-industry work. Its rounded '20 years' is not used to extend the dated 1987–2002 sequence, because it supplies no boundaries and conflicts with treating that 15-year envelope as exact continuous work. Added an undated, potentially overlapping spell so the work is not omitted. Targeted employer-name, diesel-parts, RACV contractor and Victorian inaugural-speech searches still did not identify a legal employer, weekly hours or the 1998/2000 transitions. Preserve the 27 February 2003 Victorian Hansard and historical company/personnel records as leads; totals remain uncalculable.
